objective: The owner's question of 2026-11-12 (G1, question 9; also G6, G7): nothing chooses a meeting pattern, so ask what is typical and what is rare across random ones. Under the not-all-equal law, grow meeting patterns by several random processes, each a supplied weighting (uniform knots on a fixed set of distinctions; growth with new distinctions and global closings; growth along co-knotted pairs, with overlap; growth that touches only its newest distinctions), and (a) classify fates: no allowed state, allowed states for a while then none, allowed states to the horizon; (b) read the living ones with the knots-alone line's tools (faithfulness, ties, bond distance against steps apart, shortcuts, ball growth, how far forcing reaches); (c) read the bases just before they end, and ask whether the law's relational quantities approach a limit or jump. Standalone value relative to the nearest known work: random NAE-3-SAT and hypergraph bicolouring are known for thresholds, clustering, freezing and condensation; what the allowed states read off random patterns as bond distance, and the fates of growth processes other than the uniform one, were not found in a bounded search.
stop_rule: One registered run per stage, one referee pass; report and hold.
title: Outcomes of random meeting patterns
